description: Expanded ground-truth dataset for NSBM retrieval, answerability, source matching, and evidence-grounded response evaluation. It retains the original 21 questions and adds 39 questions grounded in the collected NSBM source bundle.
evaluation_notes: The original 21 questions are retained from dataset version 1.0.
New answerable questions are grounded in the supplied NSBM PDFs and dated official website snapshots.
Page numbers are 1-based PDF pages; Markdown website snapshots use page 1.
A correct abstention is required for unanswerable questions.
The 2026 EC webpage says applications are due within 14 days; the older August 2023 EC PDF says 14 working days. These are distinct source versions and must not be conflated.
The BSc/BM/BA degree by-laws question set is explicitly historical: the file is version dated 26/7/2016 for 17.2 intake onwards. Current validity is not established.
The 2025 Faculty of Computing curriculum-revision announcement does not include the revised module-by-module curriculum.
The Data Science programme webpage is a dated public snapshot, not an approved full curriculum document. Current fees were excluded because the page showed inconsistent fee formats.
Four short or conflicted Markdown pages are archived but intentionally excluded from indexing; unsupported questions must not be answered from those pages.
Supporting-context matching should compare source basenames, because Markdown pages were ingested with absolute source paths while PDF records may use basenames.

questions.question: When can candidates enter the examination room?
questions.expected_answer: Candidates must wait until instructed by an invigilator. They are not admitted until ten minutes before the official examination commencement time or approved reading time, whichever applies.
required_facts: Admission begins ten minutes before the official commencement or approved reading time

supporting_contexts.context: Candidates shall not enter the examination room until instructed to do so by an invigilator. Candidates shall not be admitted to the examination room until ten minutes before the official time of commencement of the examination or of approved reading time, whichever is applicable.

questions.question: How late can a candidate arrive after the official examination start time?

required_facts: Maximum late admission period is thirty minutes
No additional examination time for late arrival

supporting_contexts.context: Candidates shall be admitted to the examination room up to thirty minutes after the official start of the examination, but not normally thereafter. Additional time will not be given for any candidate arriving after the start of the examination.

questions.question: How long must a candidate wait before leaving the examination hall?
questions.expected_answer: A candidate cannot leave until at least one hour has passed from the commencement of the examination. Candidates are also not allowed to leave during the final thirty minutes.
required_facts: At least one hour must pass
Cannot leave during the final thirty minutes

supporting_contexts.context: Nor shall any candidate be allowed to leave the hall until after one hour has lapsed from the commencement of the examination. No candidate is allowed to leave before the last 30 minutes of the examination.

questions.question: Which identification documents must candidates bring to the examination hall?
questions.expected_answer: Candidates must bring their Identity Card and Admission Card for every examination paper.

supporting_contexts.context: The candidate should have his/her Identity Card and the Admission Card with him/her in the hall on every occasion he/she presents himself for an Examination Paper.

questions.question: What must a candidate do before temporarily leaving the examination room?
questions.expected_answer: The candidate must obtain prior permission from an invigilator and must be accompanied by the invigilator throughout the absence.

supporting_contexts.context: If candidate wish to leave the examination room temporarily, Candidate shall seek the prior permission of an invigilator, and will be accompanied by the invigilator throughout their absence.

questions.question: Are mobile phones or other communication devices allowed in the examination room?
questions.expected_answer: No. Mobile phones and other communication devices are not permitted in the examination room.

supporting_contexts.context: A mobile ‘phone or any other communication device is not permitted into the examination room.

questions.question: With whom may candidates communicate during an examination?
questions.expected_answer: Candidates must not communicate with anyone other than an invigilator during the examination.
required_facts: Communication is restricted to an invigilator

supporting_contexts.context: During the examination Candidates shall not communicate in any way with any person other than an invigilator.

questions.question: What penalties may result from breaches of examination regulations?
